items.title: Norway's Beat Spins Out Zedoc, a New Agentic AI Platform
items.excerpt: Norway's Beat Technology has spun out Zedoc, an agentic-AI metadata platform for publishers that cleans and enriches book data, generates ONIX records, does subject classification (Thema/BISAC/Dewey), speech-to-text and audiobook chapterization to make titles discoverable to AI systems.

items.title: Can Interactive 3D Improve Digital Textbooks Without Making Reading More Complicated?
items.excerpt: Digital textbook publishers can now use AI text-to-3D tools to turn lesson descriptions into interactive 3D models, but the piece argues they should deploy the technology selectively where it clarifies spatial or internal structures that flat images cannot.

items.title: Publishing has 'lowest uptake of AI across creative industries', according to new report
items.excerpt: A new report finds book publishing has the lowest AI adoption of any creative industry at just 6%, as copyright and authorship concerns keep editorial and production teams cautious about folding generative AI into their day-to-day workflows.

items.title: Announcing a Course to Help Publishers Navigate the AI Age Responsibly
items.excerpt: Publishing Perspectives is launching 'AI in the Publishing Industry: A Workshop for Leaders and Doers,' a four-week online program teaching publishing professionals how to understand and responsibly implement AI across editorial and production workflows.

items.title: Wiley Joins 'Genesis Mission Consortium' in Support of U.S. AI Goals
items.excerpt: Wiley joined the Genesis Mission Consortium, making its AI research-intelligence tools available to Department of Energy labs alongside Nvidia and Microsoft, a sign of how scholarly publishers are turning their catalogs into AI-mediated research workflows.
